To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a plant calmodulin-like (CaM) protein, Nbrgs-Cam, functions as a suppressor of RNA silencing and is required for the activity of the geminivirus βC1 protein.
a calmodulin-like ESR is required for βC1 to function as a VSR and that the ESR is required in antiviral RNA silencing.
the plant calmodulin-like proteins are required for the functions, including silencing suppression, symptom modulation, and efficient virus infection, of a geminivirus βC1 protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between a virus and its host.
the molecular mechanisms of RNA silencing suppression by a viral satellite and its host protein, and provides new insight into the role of RDR6 in antiviral resistance
the role of a plant protein in the suppression of RNA silencing by a plant virus satellite.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
βC1, a VSR, usurps the ESR Nbrgs-CML to repress the host antiviral defense by suppressing RNA silencing.

the plant virus satellite βC1 suppresses RNA silencing by targeting the host protein Nbrgs CaM to repress RDR6 expression, which leads to suppression of secondary siRNA production and, ultimately, to virus infection.
the VSR βc1 of TYLCCNV subverts a plant ESR, the CaM-like protein NbrGS-CaM, for the purpose of suppressing host antiviral defense, which is achieved through the repression of RDR6 expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the βC1 subverts a host ESR (Nbrgs-CaMs) to suppress RNA silencing and promote virus infection, which involves βC1-induced repression of RDR6 expression and the production of secondary small interfering RNAs (siRNAs).

the βC1 protein of TYLCCNV, as a typical viral suppressor of RNA silencing, can subvert host antiviral defense by recruiting a host calmodulin-like ESR, Nbrgs-CAM, to suppress RDR6-mediated PTGS and facilitate virus replication and systemic infection.
the geminivirus βC1 usurped an endogenous calmodulin-like ESR to promote virus infection, and this ESR was required for efficient infection in both its natural hosts and in Arabidopsis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
plant viruses can exploit host ESRs to counteract host defense.
plants encode endogenous suppressor of RNA silencing, which are required for efficient viral infection and may be co-opted by viral suppressors of silencing.
plant viruses can exploit host ESRs to subvert host defense, which is an intriguing strategy of virus evolution and a novel mechanism of VSR function in plants.
